DIAGNOSIS READY: Congestive Heart Failure (likely due to a left-to-right shunt or undetected structural defect).

The normal BNP and ECG make a primary myocardial failure less likely, while the absence of fever and infectious signs rules out pneumonia. The combination of tachypnea, pitting edema, and hepatomegaly in a 3-year-old with normal liver enzymes strongly suggests chronic volume overload from a cardiac shunt. I will proceed with this diagnosis based on the clinical presentation and exclusion of other causes.
